$comment: The §4.2 dependency licence register, as DATA. Transcribed from
eclipse-player.md §4.2 (the binding requirement is REQ-GEN-012). This file is
the single source of truth; docs/THIRD-PARTY.md is generated from it by
tools/gen-third-party/gen-third-party.py and MUST NOT be hand-edited. To change
the register, edit this file, run the generator, and commit both.
A hand-written register drifts the moment a dependency changes; keeping the
register as data and regenerating on every change is what makes REQ-GEN-012's
'kept accurate' mean something a machine can check.
licence_text_policy_note: POINTER, not embedded. This build machine has no network access, so the
canonical licence texts cannot be fetched, and embedding a dozen full texts
(LGPL-3.0 alone is ~7,600 words) would bury the register they annotate. The
verbatim texts already exist in two mechanised places at package time: vcpkg
materialises each port's exact text at
to licenses/LGPL-3.0.txt per REQ-GEN-013(3). So each entry carries the SPDX id
(the canonical, machine-checkable licence identity), the SPDX text URL, and the
corresponding source URL; the generated document states plainly that the full
texts are assembled at package time and fed to the Help -> Third-Party Licences

$comment: The two facts a CycloneDX generator needs and no other consumer does.
REQ-GEN-021 wants an SBOM 'enumerating all components with SPDX licence
identifiers'; REQ-SEC-014 wants one per release artifact. Both are facts
about the dependencies, so they live here with the rest of the register
rather than in a second file that would drift away from it.
`component` is the canonical machine name — the vcpkg port name wherever
there is one, so the manifest, the resolved graph and the SBOM all spell a
component identically and a diff between them is meaningful. The display
name in `name` is for the §4.2 table and is not usable as an identifier.
gen-sbom.py FAILS if `component` is not one of the entry's own `vcpkg`
ports: it is the purl name (`pkg:vcpkg/<component>`) and the key the
resolved graph is looked up by, so a drift here would produce a purl for
a port that does not exist and a version lookup that always misses.
`scope` is CycloneDX's own enum, chosen deliberately per entry:
required  linked into the shipped artifact
optional  built only behind a feature that is off by default
excluded  in the register but not reachable at runtime
`scope_reason` is MANDATORY for optional and excluded and forbidden for
required: taking a component out of the runtime set is the one decision here
that changes what the SBOM claims was shipped, so it has to be justified in
the register rather than inferred by the generator from prose.
tools/gen-sbom.py fails if a desktop entry has no `sbom` block, so adding a
dependency cannot quietly skip the SBOM.

patent_notes.$comment: REQ-GEN-017 requires docs/THIRD-PARTY.md to record these.
items: MP3: all known essential patents expired by April 2017; decoding and encoding are unencumbered.

AAC: decoded via FFmpeg's native LGPL decoder. Patent pools exist for AAC; because we distribute source and unmodified LGPL binaries and charge nothing, we take the same position as every Linux distribution. Encoding to AAC is not offered (REQ-GEN-016).
Monkey's Audio (APE): decoded via FFmpeg's native LGPL `ape` decoder. The upstream Monkey's Audio SDK's bespoke licence MUST NOT be vendored.
DSD: decoded to PCM by FFmpeg's LGPL `dsd_*` decoders. No proprietary component.

trademark_notes.$comment: REQ-GEN-022 and REQ-GEN-023, recorded here for completeness.
items: No Winamp, AIMP, foobar2000, or other third-party trademark, logo, skin, icon, or sound asset is copied into this repository (REQ-GEN-022). Reference players are studied for design and behaviour, never for assets; built-in skins are original work.
Bundled fonts MUST be OFL-1.1, Apache-2.0, or public domain, and their licence files MUST ship alongside them (REQ-GEN-023).

entries.name: Qt 6
entries.obligation: Provide relinking ability + licence text + source offer. Static linking is FORBIDDEN (§4.3).
entries.acquisition: Official prebuilt shared libraries via aqtinstall at the version pinned in desktop/qt-version.txt. NOT a vcpkg dependency (ADR 0005 / REQ-BLD-001); desktop/vcpkg.json MUST NOT list Qt.
notes: Exact version 6.8.2 (desktop/qt-version.txt); the register names the 6.8 LTS series.
REQ-GEN-013(4) requires this document to state the exact Qt version and configure flags and link to the corresponding source archive.
REQ-GEN-013(3): the full LGPL-3.0 text ships in the installed tree at licenses/LGPL-3.0.txt and is reachable from Help -> Licences.
REQ-GEN-013(2)/(5): the user MUST be able to replace the Qt shared libraries with a compatible build; no checksum or signature gate over Qt binaries, no anti-tivoization.

entries.name: FFmpeg (libavformat, libavcodec, libavutil, libswresample)
entries.obligation: Built without `--enable-gpl` and without `--enable-nonfree` (§4.4). Publish source offer.
entries.acquisition: vcpkg, pinned by override to 7.1.2#5 in desktop/vcpkg.json (features avcodec, avformat, swresample, zlib; default features off).
notes: REQ-GEN-014 fixes the configure flags above; REQ-GEN-015 asserts at build time that the linked FFmpeg reports LGPL and not `GPL version`/`nonfree` via `avutil_license()` — a mechanical guard, not a review step (ADR 0006).
v1.0 decodes only. Encoders are enabled selectively and only for LGPL-clean codecs when the converter lands (REQ-GEN-016); `libfdk_aac` is permanently excluded as non-free.

entries.name: TagLib
entries.obligation: Source offer if the LGPL arm is chosen.
notes: Dual-licensed. Eclipse takes the LGPL-2.1-or-later arm, so the source-offer obligation applies (recorded in the companion source-offer document).

entries.name: SoundTouch
entries.acquisition: vcpkg, behind the `tempo` feature (on by default) mirroring the ECLIPSE tempo/BPM options (REQ-AUD-090..093).

entries.name: libsamplerate
notes: The ≥ 0.2.2 floor folds in two separate limits: releases before 0.1.9 were GPL and MUST NOT be used (they are incompatible with the MPL-2.0 core, §4.1), and anything below the registered version is a dependency the register does not describe, which REQ-GEN-012 makes a build failure. EclipseDependencies.cmake enforces `samplerate>=0.2.2`.

entries.name: Chromaprint
entries.acquisition: vcpkg, behind the `fingerprint` feature (on by default). Local and offline; the AcoustID network lookup is a separate opt-in (§9.9).

entries.name: projectM
entries.acquisition: vcpkg, behind the `visualizer` feature (on by default). Pulls transitive ports (see the transitive section) — glm, projectm-eval, and the OpenGL/EGL registries.
notes: ADR 0009 records the choice of projectM for MilkDrop-compatible visualisation.

entries.name: SQLite
entries.acquisition: vcpkg, with the `fts5` feature for full-text search.
notes: SQLite is dedicated to the public domain; SPDX records this as the `blessing` identifier (the 'SQLite Blessing'). No obligation, no attribution required.

entries.name: nlohmann/json

sbom.scope_reason: Carried by the §4.2 register but absent from the build: desktop/src/core/json/ is a bespoke hardened parser (ADR 0008). Nothing links it, so it is a component of no artifact.

entries.acquisition: Listed in the §4.2 register. NOT currently in the build: the desktop tree uses a bespoke, hardened in-house parser (`eclipse::json`, MPL-2.0, desktop/src/core/json/) rather than nlohmann/json, so it is registered but not linked today.
notes: Kept in the register because §4.2 lists it and REQ-GEN-012 forbids silently dropping a registered dependency; the honest status is 'registered, not linked in the current build'.

entries.name: libzip
entries.acquisition: vcpkg with `default-features: false`. The default features pull in bzip2 and OpenSSL; both are refused — REQ-THM-015 allows a skin archive only 'deflate or stored, no encryption, no other compression methods', and OpenSSL has no row in §4.2 (see OQ-025).
notes: The register offers `libzip` or `minizip-ng`; Eclipse uses libzip (BSD-3-Clause). minizip-ng would be the zlib-licensed alternative.

entries.name: GoogleTest

sbom.scope_reason: Test-only, per the §4.2 linkage column. Never linked into a shipped artifact.

entries.acquisition: vcpkg behind the `tests` feature, and pinned as a vendored tarball desktop/third_party/googletest-1.15.2.tar.gz with its SHA-256 asserted at build time. Test-only; never present in a shipped artifact.
notes: Because it is test-only and not shipped, it carries no runtime attribution or source-offer obligation.

entries.name: RtAudio
entries.licence_display: MIT-like (SPDX `MIT`; RtAudio adds a request to notify upstream of modifications)

sbom.scope_reason: Behind the `rtaudio` vcpkg feature, which is OFF by default and is a [v1.x] last-resort fallback sink (REQ-AUD-073).

entries.acquisition: vcpkg behind the `rtaudio` feature, which is OFF by default (matches the ECLIPSE_ENABLE_RTAUDIO CMake option). Optional last-resort Linux fallback sink only (REQ-AUD-073, [v1.x], §8.7.7); never bit-perfect, never a platform default.
notes: The RtAudio licence is MIT with an added request that modifications be sent upstream; there is no distinct SPDX identifier, so it is recorded as `MIT` with this note.

android.shipped_note: Listed for completeness. The Android app exists as a Phase 0 scaffold (ADR 0012 restored the target ADR 0011 had deferred) but none of these NDK-level components is in its build yet; the Gradle version catalog is reconciled with this half of the register when the components arrive (OQ-018). §0.1 rule 2 forbids silently downgrading a requirement, so the Android half is kept here and rendered, marked not-yet-shipped, rather than dropped.

$comment: Transitive vcpkg ports RECORDED IN OQ-025 as observed in one resolved graph
for x64-linux-eclipse. This is reference data transcribed from a repository
document, NOT a resolution this generator performed. When --resolved-graph is
passed, these supply licence annotations for transitive ports; ports in the
resolved graph that appear in neither the register nor this list nor
build_only_ports are unknown components and fail the gate (REQ-GEN-012, OQ-025).
vcpkg build-system helper ports. They are host/build-time tooling, never
linked into a shipped artifact, so they carry no runtime licence obligation.
Listed so that, when they appear in a resolved graph, they are classified
rather than flagged as unknown components.
